subject: Penetration summary and remediation status for procurement gating (MoveFast)
messages:
From: James Tan <james.tan@movefast.io>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-30T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Penetration test report and remediation summary required for procurement gating

Hi Dylan,

We're in the final stages for procurement and our security team needs the latest penetration test outputs and a short remediation summary to gate the purchase order. Our MAP cutoff is 2026-07-07; procurement can't move forward without the following by next Friday: 1) a redacted penetration test report or executive summary we can share internally, 2) a remediation tracker showing status for all HIGH/CRITICAL findings (fixed / in progress / accepted), and 3) confirmation whether a retest is scheduled and what scope it covers.

Specific asks:
- Exec summary or redacted PDF (no vendor-sensitive exploit code).
- A CSV/Spreadsheet with issue IDs, severity, CVE (if applicable), current status, owner, and mitigation ETA.
- Signed attestation that third-party dependencies were included in the assessment or clearly called out if excluded.

Can you confirm whether you can provide those artifacts and whether you can meet our timeline? If you need to escalate for an exception we may be able to extend the gate by 48 hours, but we prefer not to.

Thanks,
James
Procurement | MoveFast Inc.
Attachment: movefast-sig-questions-v3.xlsx (questionnaire)

Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Penetration test report and remediation summary required for procurement gating

Hi team — quick technical summary and what we'll deliver.

Scope and artifacts:
- Assessment: External network + authenticated webapp + critical API endpoints + dependency scan (SCA). Internal-only services excluded (per contract).
- Deliverables we will make available to MoveFast: a redacted executive summary PDF (no PoC exploit code, no raw stack traces), a remediation tracker CSV export from our vuln tracker, and a limited evidence bundle (screenshots, sanitized request/response extracts). Full raw logs and internal test scaffolding are considered internal and will not be released.

Remediation status (current snapshot):
- Total confirmed findings: 42
- HIGH: 5 (4 fixed, 1 in progress — patch queued for 2026-07-08)
- CRITICAL: 1 (mitigated via temporary WAF rule, scheduled for code fix 2026-07-15)
- MEDIUM/LOW: remainder tracked, bulk rolled into the next sprint.

Percent complete for HIGH/CRITICAL: ~83% mitigation (4/6 fully fixed or mitigated). We will include a per-issue owner and ETA column in the remediation spreadsheet.

Retest: We can run a targeted retest for the remaining HIGH/CRITICAL items the week of 2026-07-06 and provide a short retest summary by 2026-07-10. If MoveFast requires an independent third-party revalidation, we will coordinate procurement and share timing.

Redaction process:
- We will remove exploit code, internal hostnames, and any proprietary test harness output. We can provide an unredacted report under NDA if MoveFast legal requires — please advise.

Attachments to be delivered with exec summary package: redwood-pt-full-executive-summary-20260630.pdf, vuln-tracker-export-MF-1173.csv.

Let me know if that covers MoveFast's asks or if they need the unredacted package under NDA.

—Marissa
Security Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
From: James Tan <james.tan@movefast.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@movefast.io
Date: 2026-07-01T11:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Penetration test report and remediation summary required for procurement gating

Marissa — thanks, that level of detail helps. Couple quick clarifications before we close the gate:

1) Can you confirm the CVE identifiers for the HIGH/CRITICAL items (if assigned)? We need CVE references where applicable for our internal risk scoring.
2) Were transitive dependencies (package-level SCA findings) included in the remediation tracker or are those a separate export?
3) For the CRITICAL item you noted as mitigated by WAF, please indicate whether the mitigation is considered temporary (we would treat temporary mitigations differently in our scoring).

We prefer redacted materials inside our procurement system. If you can get the exec summary + CSV by 7/02 EOD and the evidence Drive link by 7/03, procurement will proceed to issue the PO and DocuSign. If you prefer, we can accept a signed attestation that third-party dependencies were reviewed and a separate CSV of SCA findings.

Attaching an updated SIG question set for your team to mark scope/exclusions: movefast-sig-questions-v3.xlsx

Thanks — I will loop security ops if we need an unredacted package under NDA.

James

James — closing the loop. Deliverables and next steps:

1) Redacted executive summary (redwood-pt-full-executive-summary-20260630.pdf) — uploaded: https://drive.google.com/redwood-share/pt/MF-1173 (shared link, view-only).
2) Remediation spreadsheet (vuln-tracker-export-MF-1173.csv and XLSX export) — includes CVE column where assigned and per-issue owner + ETA. Transitive SCA findings were included in a separate sheet in the export.
3) Evidence bundle (sanitized screenshots & request/response extracts) — included in the Drive link. Raw logs are internal only; available under NDA.
4) Retest window: Targeting 2026-07-06 to 2026-07-09 for the remaining HIGH/CRITICAL items; retest summary by 2026-07-10.
5) CRITICAL WAF mitigation: marked as temporary in the tracker; full code fix ETA 2026-07-15.

If MoveFast is comfortable with the redacted package we will expect procurement to proceed. HubSpot deal HS-9876543 will be updated and we'll send the DocuSign PO link once procurement notifies us. DocuSign PO placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/po/MF-2026-1173
